# logmoji

> Small Node.js logger with emojis. Each log line gets an emoji and a level label, with log levels, minimum-level and allowlist filtering, console log colors (ANSI codes), timestamps and context loggers.

Install with `npm install logmoji`. The package exports a factory, not a logger: call `require("logmoji")({ timestamp: false })` in CommonJS, or `import createLogger from "logmoji"` and then `createLogger(options)` in ESM. Set `LOGMOJI_DISABLE=true` in the environment to silence all output.

## Docs

- [Home](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/): overview
- [Usage](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/usage.html): Node.js logging setup, every log function, context loggers and level filtering
- [Configuration](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/config.html): timestamps, date formats, minLevel, levels, custom emojis and console log colors
- [Console log colors picker](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/console-log-colors/): pick an ANSI color per log level, preview it and copy the logColors config

## Blog

- [Blog index](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/): Node.js logging guides
- [Log levels explained](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/log-levels-explained.html): what debug, info, warn, error and fatal mean
- [Log level hierarchy](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/log-level-hierarchy.html): severity order, syslog vs pino numbering, thresholds
- [Pino logger](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/pino-logger.html): pino setup, levels, child loggers, pino-pretty, redaction
- [Winston logger](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/winston-logger.html): winston setup, levels, formats and transports
- [Winston vs pino](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/winston-vs-pino.html): documented features side by side, with a console logger
- [Color console.log in Node.js](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/console-log-colors-node.html): ANSI escape codes, util.styleText, isTTY and NO_COLOR
- [Node.js logging basics](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/nodejs-logging-basics.html): console methods, timestamps, levels and context for small apps
- [Emoji logs](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/emoji-console-logs.html): one emoji, label and color per level in logmoji
- [What Date.prototype.toISOString returns, and when it throws](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/toisostring.html): How toISOString formats a JavaScript date: always UTC with a Z, extended years, the RangeError for invalid dates, toJSON, and local time strings for log files.
- [Structured logs: why logs became JSON, with Node.js output](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/structured-logging.html): What structured logging means, what a JSON log line looks like in pino and winston, which fields to include, and when plain text console logs are enough.
- [What console.error does differently from console.log](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/console-error.html): What console.error does in Node.js and the browser: stderr vs stdout, format strings, Error objects, redirecting with 2> and 2>&1, and logmoji's error levels.
- [Turning debug output on and off with the debug package](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/debug-npm.html): How the debug npm package works: namespaces, the DEBUG variable, wildcards and exclusions, stderr output, TTY timestamps, %o formatting and DEBUG_COLORS.
- [Reading and managing Node.js logs under pm2](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/pm2-logs.html): How pm2 logs works: where pm2 keeps out and error files, --lines and --nostream, adding timestamps with --time or log_date_format, flush and log rotation.
- [Printing nested objects in full with console.dir](https://projects.halit.org/logmoji/blog/console-dir.html): How console.dir prints objects in Node.js and how it differs from console.log: depth, colors and showHidden options, depth null, circular refs and util.inspect.
